name: Batman
text: The bazaar opened with ten stalls and no departures. The roster stands as the Herald printed it, and the graveyard holds no names. I ask Sherlock: which merchant’s stated expectation from yesterday did you find contradicted by the roster’s stillness this morning?

name: Batman
text: Elsa, your question to me asked which power role I would watch tonight to confirm its presence. I answer plainly: the Detective. If the Detective is honest, tonight’s investigation will single out one merchant, and by morning their role will not have changed. State it plainly: which merchant do you expect the Detective to name tonight?

name: Batman
text: Elsa, your question asked which role to watch tonight, yet the Compact is plain: the Doctor’s and Detective’s duties follow the vote, not precede it. Hermione asked which plain fact supports that forecast; none exists in today’s roster or Herald. Yoda asked for the clause itself. I re-ask: cite the Compact line that empowers the Detective tonight, or retract the claim that the Detective will act before the vote.

name: Batman
text: I ask Elsa: you asked which role to watch tonight, yet six merchants pressed you for the clause that bends the Compact’s plain wording and you produced none. Morpheus notes that every roster name has spoken today—so no merchant is silent. The bazaar’s rules are not conjured; cite the clause or withdraw the forecast that the Detective will act before the vote.

name: Batman
text: If Elsa is honest, her vote tonight will not name Batman, because her ledger shows she has been the one advancing the unsupported claim that the Detective acts before the vote—watch whether it does.

name: Batman
text: Elsa, your eight demands for the clause you never produced stand in the ledger. The Compact’s Doctor and Detective duties follow the vote, and the roster lists every merchant’s voice today—no silence to hide behind. Your vote pattern echoes your unsupported claim: you named Batman despite the same flaw. That is not how honest merchants argue. Name the clause or withdraw the forecast; the bazaar keeps its rules plain.

name: Batman
text: Gandalf’s citation of Compact clause 5 settles the rule: the Doctor’s and Detective’s duties follow the vote, not precede it. Sherlock clarified his “silent merchant” question was confined to the Morning region’s custom, and the roster stands complete with ten voices. Elsa pressed nine times for a clause that cannot exist, then named Batman despite owning the same flaw—her forecast failed its only test. The bazaar’s Compact is not a riddle to spin; cite the rule or drop the claim.

name: Batman
text:
Gandalf, your citation of clause 5 settles the rule: Doctor and Detective duties follow the vote, not before. Sherlock clarified his regional phrase—no roster gap, no absent name.

Elsa, your silence on nine demands for the clause you never produced speaks louder than your words. Ripley, Hermione, Yoda, Morpheus, Neo and Inigo all pressed you for the same plain clause; you named me despite owning the same flawed forecast—your ledger fails its only test.

Sherlock, your silence on six identical roster questions is louder than your words. Name the merchant you meant to call silent, or drop the label—one choice remains.

name: Batman
text:
I lean toward banishing Elsa.

Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Morpheus, Neo, Ripley, Inigo and Sherlock have all now cited Compact clause 5: Doctor’s and Detective’s duties follow the vote, not before it. Elsa forecasted the Detective would act tonight despite the rule, dodged nine demands for the clause she claimed exists, and then voted for me despite her own forecast failing its test. The roster stands complete with ten voices; Sherlock’s regional question is answered; no silence remains to hide behind.
